name: Booker T. & the M.G.'s
hook: The Stax house band: two Black and two white musicians in segregated Memphis, who had a hit by jamming while waiting for a singer and then played on hundreds of soul records.

blurb.age13: Booker T. & the M.G.'s were the house band at Stax Records in Memphis. In summer 1962, 17-year-old organist Booker T. Jones, guitarist Steve Cropper, bassist Lewie Steinberg and drummer Al Jackson Jr. were waiting in the studio for a singer who did not turn up, and started jamming on an organ riff. That jam became 'Green Onions', a top-three hit. The band had two Black members and two white members at a time when Memphis was segregated, which made them one of the first racially integrated groups in American pop. They played on hundreds of records by Otis Redding, Wilson Pickett, Sam & Dave and others, and helped create the sound of Southern soul. Al Jackson Jr. was murdered in 1975. Booker T. Jones later produced Willie Nelson's album 'Stardust'.
blurb.adult: Formed in Memphis in 1962 as the core of the Stax house band: Booker T. Jones (organ), Steve Cropper (guitar), Lewie Steinberg (bass, replaced by Donald 'Duck' Dunn in 1965) and Al Jackson Jr. (drums). 'Green Onions' came from a jam on a Sunday in June 1962 when a session with Billy Lee Riley did not happen; Jim Stewart wanted 'Behave Yourself' as the A-side, but Cropper and Memphis DJs pushed the other side, and it reached number one R&B and number three pop. With two Black and two white members, they were one of the first racially integrated rock groups, in a city and a genre then seen as Black. As the Stax rhythm section they played on 'I've Been Loving You Too Long', 'Try a Little Tenderness', 'Hold On, I'm Comin'' and 'Soul Man', and with Motown's Funk Brothers are credited with originating much of the sound of soul. Jackson was murdered in 1975; Dunn died in 2012 and Cropper in December 2025. Jones produced Willie Nelson's 'Stardust' (1978).
